summary_paragraph: A woman with advanced AIDS (CD4 22, high viral load, not on HAART), ESRD on thrice-weekly hemodialysis via femoral tunneled catheter, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was admitted with left groin pain, swelling, warmth, and purulent drainage at her femoral dialysis catheter site. The infected left femoral catheter was removed and cultures from the wound/catheter tip and one blood culture grew MRSA; she was treated with IV vancomycin with subsequent surveillance blood cultures showing no further growth, and a new tunneled catheter was placed after a 3-day line holiday. Her course was complicated by C. difficile diarrhea treated with a 14-day course of oral metronidazole, and by malposition of the new right femoral catheter traversing a small atrial septal defect into the left atrium with a possible small catheter-tip thrombus; she received a heparin infusion with repeat TEE showing resolution and the catheter was exchanged for a shorter line under radiologic guidance. She restarted antiretroviral therapy (abacavir, atazanavir/ritonavir, and renally dosed emtricitabine) and continued opportunistic infection prophylaxis. She was discharged home with services to continue vancomycin dosed after dialysis (MWF) to complete a 3-week course, finish metronidazole for C. difficile, continue dialysis via the right femoral catheter, and follow closely with her HIV and dialysis teams.
problems: MRSA femoral hemodialysis catheter infection with MRSA bacteremia
End stage renal disease on hemodialysis; tunneled catheter removal and replacement
Malpositioned hemodialysis catheter traversing atrial septal defect with suspected catheter-tip thrombus; treated with heparin and catheter exchange
Clostridioides difficile infection treated with metronidazole
Advanced HIV/AIDS; antiretroviral therapy restarted; continued opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (remained in sinus rhythm; anticoagulation discussed but not started)
Right V1 post-herpetic neuralgia/headache (stable on duloxetine)
